cards.name: Bend
cards.summary: Legacy Premiere distortion that runs travelling waves through the frame horizontally and vertically, so the picture ripples and bends like a flag or a reflection in water. The waves move on their own over time, without keyframes.
use_for: Dream / flashback wobble on an archive photo
Fake heat haze or underwater ripple on b-roll
Comic 'drunk' wobble on a satire reaction shot
avoid: Choosing it over Wave Warp or Turbulent Displace: it is CPU-only legacy code with a setup dialog, and parts of its harvest are unreliable
Strong intensity on faces looks cheap
Frame edges pull in and reveal the fill colour or transparency

params.name: Horizontal Intensity
params.does: Height of the horizontal waves (how far pixels move)

cards.scripting: Bend is not in the Premiere 2026 Effects panel as far as can be told (Adobe's 26.0 effect lists and Distort docs do not mention it), but it is still in the QE effect list, so it can be applied by name from a script. That status is not confirmed: use Wave Warp for new edits. 'Horizontal/Vertical Frequency' and 'Horizontal/Vertical Source' have unclamped harvested ranges (+/-1e9) and are probably the setup-dialog popups (wave direction / wave type), so do not set them. 'Fill Color' is exposed as a number with a broken harvested range (min > max), so do not set it either. If you use Bend anyway, set the Intensity, Rate and Width rows only. The default 15 intensity already animates; the demo uses 25 on both axes.

verified.note: Obsolete card but frame 000 was rendered: strong horizontal and vertical waves bend the whole shot into a liquid swirl, stripes and figures warped into S-curves.

cards.name: Color Balance (RGB)
cards.summary: Scales the red, green and blue channels independently to shift the overall colour cast. It is a fast, simple white-balance or tint correction.
use_for: Quickly warm up a cold archive or phone clip
Cool / blue cast for a tense or night segment in a documentary
Neutralise a green or magenta cast on mixed press footage before Lumetri
Strong colour wash for a flashback (one channel high, the others low)
avoid: Big pushes clip the highlights of that channel and look cheap; use Lumetri Color for real grading
It is believed to scale (gain) each channel, so pure black would stay black and a tint in lifted shadows cannot be removed: use Lumetri Color or Levels for shadow casts

params.name: Green
params.typical: 235-275; lower to remove a green cast

params.name: Blue
params.typical: 200-280; lower to warm, raise to cool

cards.scripting: These are harvested internal units: 0..510, with 255 = no change. Effect Controls shows 0-200 % with 100 as the default, so internal = UI x 2.55. That conversion is inferred from the default and the range, not tested on screen. Keep all three near 255 for corrections. Moving only one channel above 300 gives an obvious cast.

verified.note: Strong warm orange cast over the whole shot (mean R 129->187, B 63->37, G unchanged), a clear channel-scaled tint.

cards.name: Color Replace
cards.summary: Replaces every pixel close to a chosen Target Color with a new Replace Color, keeping the original shading (or a flat fill with Solid Colors). Similarity sets how wide a range of shades is matched.
use_for: Recolour a flag, banner or t-shirt to another colour for a satire beat
Swap a plain background wall colour in an explainer shot
Turn an orange sunset sky green or purple for a surreal trailer moment
avoid: High Similarity bleeds into skin tones and the whole frame
Noisy or compressed footage gives speckled, flickering edges; Lumetri HSL Secondary is cleaner
Recolouring real news footage can mislead viewers: only for clearly labelled satire or explainer graphics

params.name: Target Color
params.typical: sampled from the actual frame, e.g. a flag red

params.name: Similarity
params.does: Tolerance: how far from Target Color a pixel can be and still be replaced

params.name: Solid Colors
params.does: true = flat fill with no shading, false = keep the original shading

cards.scripting: Matching is global by RGB distance. For a real job, sample Target Color from a frame of the clip: a guessed colour may match nothing. The demo Target Color #903C1A is the stripe / desk red sampled from the gallery test clip (test_a.mp4 at 2 s), so the stripes turn green; a pure red such as #C8282D barely occurs in that footage. Similarity is in harvested units 0..127, and how they map to the UI percentage is not verified. To limit the swap to one object, add a mask on the effect (masks cannot come from a spec). Colours are "#RRGGBB"; the harvest stores them as packed 64-bit ints.

verified.note: Warm/dark tones (clothing, foreground blocks, stripes, wall shadows) are swapped to green with their shading kept while faces and the light wall stay, an obvious surreal recolour.

cards.name: Gamma Correction
cards.summary: Brightens or darkens the midtones while leaving the deepest blacks and brightest whites largely in place. It has one slider, and 10 means no change.
use_for: Lift a dark interview or phone clip without blowing the highlights
Darken the midtones for a moody documentary reconstruction or trailer shot
Quickly match brightness between archive clips
avoid: Extremes (1-3 or 24-28) flatten or crush the image and look cheap
It does not fix colour casts or contrast: use Levels or Lumetri Color for those

params.name: Gamma
params.does: Midtone curve: 10 = neutral; values below 10 are believed to brighten the midtones and values above 10 to darken them
params.typical: 7-13 for corrections, 18-22 for a moody look

cards.scripting: Range 1..28 and default 10 come from the harvest. The direction (lower = lighter) is from memory of the Adobe docs and is not verified: check one rendered frame before relying on it. It is safe to keyframe for a slow exposure drift.

verified.note: Gamma 20 darkens the midtones (mean RGB 129/102/63 -> 76/48/21) into a moody saturated brown while the brightest wall areas hold.

cards.name: Extract
cards.summary: Turns the clip into pure black and white: pixels whose brightness falls between Black Input Level and White Input Level become white and the rest become black, with Softness adding grey gradation at the boundary. The result is a stark stencil or threshold image.
use_for: Stencil / poster treatment of a leader's photo for a title card
Graphic black-and-white background behind lower thirds or quotes
Quick luma-matte source for Track Matte Key
One- or two-frame flash frames in a trailer or meme reel
avoid: A narrow range with low Softness gives noisy, blotchy faces
It is not a tasteful black-and-white grade: use Black & White or Lumetri saturation 0 for that

params.name: Black Input Level
params.does: Lower brightness bound; darker pixels become black

params.name: White Input Level
params.does: Upper brightness bound; brighter pixels also become black

params.name: Softness
params.does: Grey gradation at the boundaries (0 = hard threshold)

params.name: Invert
params.does: Swaps the black and white result

cards.scripting: Do not confuse it with After Effects' 'Extract', which is a channel/luma KEY that makes pixels transparent. Premiere's Extract outputs an opaque black-and-white image. Levels are 0..255 8-bit units; keep White Input Level > Black Input Level. Add Tint after it for a two-colour (party-colour) stencil.

verified.note: Shot becomes a stark black-and-white threshold stencil: light wall white, dark clothing and foreground blocks black, soft grey at the boundaries.

cards.name: Color Pass
cards.summary: Keeps one chosen colour (and the shades near it) and turns everything else greyscale, the classic 'colour splash' or Sin City look. Reverse does the opposite: it greys out only the chosen colour.
use_for: Keep only a party flag's colour in a crowd or rally shot
Highlight a red file or object in a documentary reconstruction
Noir flashback where one key object stays in colour
Trailer 'blood red' accent beat
avoid: High Similarity lets skin and other colours through and the look collapses
Compressed footage makes the kept colour's edges flicker; Lumetri HSL Secondary is cleaner

params.name: Color
params.typical: sampled flag / object colour, e.g. #903C1A (the test clip's stripe red)

params.name: Similarity
params.does: How wide a range of shades around Color survives
params.typical: 10-25 on warm footage; at 40 most warm tones (skin, wall, foreground blocks) survived on the test clip (harvested range 0..127)

params.name: Reverse
params.does: true = grey out only the chosen colour and keep the rest

cards.scripting: Even when the chosen colour is absent, the frame still turns grey, so the effect is always visible. Sample Color from the real clip for a clean result: the demo #903C1A is the stripe red sampled from the gallery test clip, but on this warm clip Similarity 40 kept almost everything in colour (only the lightest wall greyed), so the demo uses 15. Similarity is in harvested units 0..127, and how they map to the UI is unverified. The 'colour drains away' recipe starts at 120 (nearly everything kept, since 40 already kept most colours) and ends at the demo value 15, not 35: on the test clip 35-40 still leaves most of the frame in colour, so the drain would never land on the splash look.

verified.note: Re-rendered at Similarity 15: the frame is greyscale except the red stripes, skin and flowers, a clear colour-splash look (mean saturation 136 -> 12).

cards.name: Lens Distortion
cards.summary: Simulates or corrects lens curvature: positive Curvature bulges the image outward (convex, barrel / fisheye) and negative Curvature pinches it (concave, pincushion), with optional off-centre and prism skew. Uncovered areas become transparent or are filled with Fill Color.
use_for: Remove GoPro / drone / action-cam fisheye: negative Curvature (start around -30 to -50) straightens the bowed lines
Fake fisheye bulge on a meme or reaction close-up
Warp-zoom punch transition when Curvature is keyframed across a cut
Slight curvature on screen recordings for a retro CRT look
avoid: Large values on faces look cartoonish unless that is the joke

Strong positive Curvature shrinks the picture into a rounded barrel and exposes the frame edges and corners (filled white with default settings in the gallery render): scale the clip up ~120-140 % or set Fill Color

params.name: Curvature
params.does: Amount of lens bend: positive = convex bulge (barrel / fisheye), negative = concave pinch (pincushion, also removes fisheye)

params.name: Fill Alpha
params.does: Harvested default true; with that default the gallery render filled the uncovered area with Fill Color (white), not transparency, so what true/false do is unverified

params.name: Fill Color
params.does: Colour of the uncovered area around the distorted picture (default white)

cards.scripting: Sign convention per Adobe's documentation: positive Curvature makes the image convex (bulge / fisheye), negative makes it concave (pincushion), which is why fisheye removal uses negative values. Checked on a rendered frame: +60 gives a convex barrel that pulls the picture in from all four edges. With the default Fill settings the uncovered area rendered white (the default Fill Color), not transparent/black. For the punch transition, keyframe both clips around the cut, or place it on an adjustment layer spanning the cut.

verified.note: Curvature 60 pulls the picture into a convex barrel shape with bowed edges, and the uncovered surround is filled white (default Fill Color).

cards.name: Levels
cards.summary: Classic input/output levels for the composite RGB and for each channel separately. It remaps the black point, white point and gamma to fix contrast, crush or lift blacks, or tint shadows and highlights per channel.
use_for: Fix flat or washed-out press / phone footage by setting the black and white input points
Faded 'archive' look by raising (RGB) Black Output Level
Tint the shadows (e.g. blue/teal) per channel for a cinematic documentary look
Match exposure between interview angles
avoid: Black input above ~60 or white input below ~190 crushes or clips detail
Per-channel moves without checking a scope give odd skin tones

params.name: (RGB) Black Input Level
params.does: Input value that becomes black (crushes shadows)

params.name: (RGB) White Input Level
params.does: Input value that becomes white (brightens highlights)

cards.scripting: All levels are 8-bit 0..255 values. Gamma rows are x100 (100 = 1.0, range 0..1000). As in After Effects, gamma above 100 should brighten the midtones, but that is not verified. Rows are prefixed (RGB), (R), (G), (B); use those exact names. Premiere's histogram setup dialog cannot be reached from a script, and it is not needed.

verified.note: Punchier contrast with crushed blacks and brighter highlights, and the lifted blue output gives the dark clothing a cool tint (mean B up while R/G drop).

cards.name: ASC CDL
cards.summary: Applies an ASC Color Decision List primary grade: per-channel Slope (gain), Offset (lift) and Power (gamma), plus overall Saturation. CDL is the standard numeric format for carrying a look between grading tools.
use_for: Apply CDL numbers received from a colourist or DIT to match a series look
Fast numeric primary grade (warm highlights, cooler shadows) for a documentary
Boost the saturation of dull press footage
Store a reusable channel look as plain numbers in a spec
avoid: Offsets are strong: +/-0.05 is already a clear shift and most of the +/-10 range is unusable
Power far from 1 bands or posterises 8-bit footage

params.name: Red Offset
params.does: Red lift added to all levels (0 = neutral)

cards.equivalent: OCIO CDL Transform (reads a .cc/.cdl file) or Lumetri Color
cards.scripting: Values are plain floats. Slope and Power are neutral at 1, Offset at 0, Saturation at 1. The ASC formula is out = (in x slope + offset) ^ power, followed by saturation. After Effects has no numeric ASC CDL effect: its OCIO CDL Transform applies a .cc/.cdl file instead, and Lumetri Color is the closest hand-set grade. Pasted CDL triples map in R, G, B order to the Red/Green/Blue rows.

verified.note: Strong warm orange primary grade with boosted saturation (mean R 129->191, B 63->22, saturation 136->229), as described.

cards.name: Alpha Adjust
cards.summary: Changes how a clip's alpha channel is used: scale its opacity, ignore the embedded alpha, invert it, or show only the matte. On an opaque live-action clip it simply makes the clip see-through.
use_for: Invert a logo or graphic alpha to cut a 'window' together with Track Matte Key
Ignore the bad alpha of an imported PNG / ProRes 4444 graphic
Mask Only to check a key or a graphic's matte during QC
Set the opacity of a keyed overlay after the keyer, independently of the clip's Opacity
avoid: On opaque footage Invert Alpha makes the whole clip vanish
For a simple fade it duplicates the built-in Opacity property: use Opacity keyframes instead

params.name: Ignore Alpha
params.does: Treats the clip as fully opaque

params.name: Invert Alpha
params.typical: false; true to punch a window

params.name: Mask Only
params.does: Shows the alpha as a white-on-black image

cards.scripting: How visible the result is depends on what lies underneath: it is black when the track below is empty. Effect order matters: place it after a keyer (Ultra Key, Luma Key) to adjust the key's result. In After Effects the same job is done by layer Opacity, Set Matte or Invert (Channel: Alpha).

verified.note: Opacity 40 makes the opaque clip see-through over the empty black track, so the shot renders at about 40% brightness (mean RGB 129/102/63 -> 50/40/24).

cards.name: Alpha Glow
cards.summary: Adds a coloured glow that radiates outward from the edges of a clip's alpha channel, for example around text, a logo or a keyed subject. A full-frame opaque clip has no alpha edges, so nothing shows. In Premiere 26 it sits in the Legacy folder.
use_for: Neon halo around title or lower-third text in a reel
Glow around a cut-out leader photo (PNG or keyed) in an explainer
Aura on a logo in an end card
avoid: New edits: it is a Legacy (CPU) effect in Premiere 26; use Drop Shadow with Distance 0 and high Softness for an alpha-edge glow
Full-frame live-action footage: no visible change
A large Glow with saturated colours looks dated (2000s WordArt)

params.name: Glow
params.does: How far the glow extends from the alpha edge

params.name: Brightness
params.does: Initial opacity / strength of the glow

params.name: End Color
params.does: Colour the glow fades to (used only when the unnamed 'Use End Color' toggle is on)

cards.scripting: Legacy effect, kept for old projects. The current replacement for an alpha-edge glow is Drop Shadow with Distance 0, a high Softness and a bright Shadow Color; Edge Glow and Wonder Glow are highlight blooms, not alpha-edge glows. If you still use Alpha Glow, apply it to a clip with transparency: a title / graphic, a PNG cut-out, footage after Ultra Key, or a nested clip that is scaled down. Settings for such a clip: {"Glow": 40, "Brightness": 255, "Start Color": "#FFD400"}. The two unnamed bool rows (harvest name "") are believed to be 'Use End Color' and 'Fade Out', in that order. They cannot be addressed by name, so leave them at their defaults. The closest After Effects effect is Glow with Glow Based On: Alpha Channel.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (a full-frame opaque clip has no alpha edges to glow), so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Auto Reframe
cards.summary: Adobe Sensei analyses the clip and pans / zooms it to keep the main action in frame when the sequence has a different aspect ratio from the footage (e.g. 16:9 footage in a 9:16 reel sequence). It writes the path it finds into generated keyframes, and the Reframe Offset / Scale / Rotation rows let you tweak it.
use_for: Turn 16:9 press or interview footage into 9:16 reels while keeping the speaker centred
Square 1:1 cut-downs of news clips
Quick vertical version of a documentary trailer
avoid: In a sequence with the same aspect ratio as the clip it does nothing
Fast multi-person shots make it hunt between faces: fix with Adjust Position or manual keyframes
Burned-in lower thirds and tickers in the source get cropped off: reframe clean footage

params.name: Motion Tracking
params.does: How quickly the reframe follows the action (dropdown)

params.name: Reframe Scale
params.does: Extra zoom on top of the analysed framing (100 = as analysed)

params.name: Reframe Offset
params.does: Manual offset of the analysed framing

params.name: Adjust Position
params.does: Manual position override of the reframed path

cards.scripting: It only does something when the sequence aspect differs from the clip, and it needs its own analysis pass, which runs in the background after the effect is applied: wait before rendering. The better scripted route is the ExtendScript call Sequence.autoReframeSequence(numerator, denominator, 'slower'|'default'|'faster', newName, useNestedSequences) on the finished 16:9 sequence. It creates a new reframed sequence with Auto Reframe already applied to every clip. Never set the internal rows ' ' (blank name), 'Hash arb data', 'Generated Keyframes', 'Scale (Auto Generated)' or 'Overwrite generated path'. The units of Reframe Offset are unverified. After Effects has no equivalent effect: reframe there with Transform or Position keyframes.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input (needs a sequence aspect different from the clip plus an analysis pass), so no gallery frame was rendered.
